_about: Offline quiz questions for MNEMO_FAKE=1 (see FakeLLM._quiz_item). One per second-level topic. choice: [question, correct option, three wrong options]; short: [question, model answer, keywords the fake grader looks for, alternatives separated by |].

choice: What does Gödel's first incompleteness theorem say about any consistent, effectively axiomatised theory that contains basic arithmetic?
It contains true statements it cannot prove
It can prove its own consistency
Every statement in it is decidable
short: What does it mean for a problem to be undecidable?
No algorithm gives the correct yes/no answer for every instance; the halting problem is the classic example.

choice: By Lagrange's theorem, the order of a subgroup of a finite group always…
divides the order of the group
equals the number of conjugacy classes
is half the order of the group
short: What is an eigenvector of a linear map?
A non-zero vector the map only rescales: A v = λ v, with λ its eigenvalue.

choice: Which property of the real numbers distinguishes them from the rationals?
Every bounded non-empty set has a least upper bound
short: What does uniform convergence add to pointwise convergence?
The same N works for every point at once, so the sup of the error goes to zero; limits of continuous functions stay continuous.

choice: Why is a coffee mug topologically the same as a doughnut?
Each can be continuously deformed into the other; both have one hole
short: What does Gauss's Theorema Egregium say about curvature?
Gaussian curvature is intrinsic: it can be measured from distances within the surface, so it is preserved by isometries.

choice: Fermat's little theorem says that for a prime p and an integer a not divisible by p…
short: Roughly how many primes are there below a large number N?
About N / ln N, by the prime number theorem.

choice: A connected graph has an Eulerian circuit exactly when…
it has as many edges as vertices
short: If more than n objects go into n boxes, some box holds at least two.

choice: What does the central limit theorem say about the mean of many i.i.d. variables with finite variance?
Its distribution approaches a normal distribution
Its variance grows with the sample size
short: The probability, assuming the null hypothesis is true, of data at least as extreme as what was observed.

choice: What is the worst-case time complexity of comparison-based sorting?
short: What does it mean for a problem to be NP-complete?
It is in NP and every problem in NP reduces to it in polynomial time.

choice: no player gains by changing strategy alone
every player gets the highest possible payoff
short: Why is convexity so valuable in optimisation?
In a convex problem every local minimum is a global minimum, so local methods find the optimum.

choice: Who developed calculus independently of Newton, introducing the dx notation still used today?
short: What did Euclid's Elements establish as a way of doing mathematics?
Deriving theorems from a small set of axioms and postulates by proof.

choice: Noether's theorem links conservation of energy to which symmetry?
short: What do Maxwell's equations predict about light?
That it is an electromagnetic wave travelling at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀).

choice: In the canonical ensemble, the probability of a microstate with energy E is proportional to…
short: The power with which a quantity diverges or vanishes near a continuous phase transition, e.g. ξ ∼ |T − Tc|^(−ν); it is universal.

choice: What does the Pauli exclusion principle forbid?
Two identical fermions occupying the same quantum state
Two bosons occupying the same state
Measuring position and momentum at all
short: A joint state of several systems that cannot be written as a product of individual states, giving correlations stronger than any classical ones.

choice: What does the equivalence principle state?
Locally, gravity is indistinguishable from acceleration
All inertial frames see the same speed of light
short: What is the cosmic microwave background?
Relic radiation from when the universe became transparent, about 380,000 years after the Big Bang, now cooled to about 2.7 K.

choice: Hydrogen fusing into helium in its core
short: How do astronomers usually detect exoplanets?
By the dip in a star's light as a planet transits, or by the star's Doppler wobble.

choice: What does a catalyst do to a reaction?
Lowers the activation energy without being consumed
Shifts the equilibrium towards the products
Is used up to drive it forward
short: What makes a bond covalent rather than ionic?
Electrons are shared between atoms rather than transferred from one to the other.

choice: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
Convection in the mantle and slab pull
short: How does the greenhouse effect warm the Earth?
Gases such as CO₂ and water vapour absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit it, partly back towards the surface.

choice: In the central dogma, what does a ribosome do?
short: What is the role of mitochondria?
They produce most of the cell's ATP through respiration.

choice: Random change in allele frequencies, strongest in small populations
short: What does natural selection need in order to work?
Heritable variation in traits that affects survival or reproduction.
How does a vaccine protect you?
It trains the immune system with a harmless antigen so that it responds quickly to the real pathogen.

choice: What carries a signal across a chemical synapse?
An electrical current through gap proteins
short: A brief all-or-nothing spike in a neuron's membrane voltage that travels down the axon.

choice: Where does the optic nerve leave the eye?
At the blind spot, where there are no photoreceptors
short: Why do we see depth with two eyes?
Each eye sees from a slightly different position, and the brain uses the disparity between the images.

choice: Roughly how many items can working memory hold at once?
About four (Miller's old estimate was seven, plus or minus two)
short: Judging how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.

choice: Which brain structure is most associated with fear?
short: What is the difference between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation?
Intrinsic motivation comes from the activity itself; extrinsic from outside rewards or pressures.

choice: knowing that things exist when out of sight
the ability to sort objects by size
short: The bond an infant forms with a caregiver, which provides a secure base and shapes later relationships.

choice: What did Asch's line experiments show?
People often conform to a group's obviously wrong answer
People obey authority figures to harm others
Groups make better decisions than individuals
short: People are less likely to help in an emergency when others are present.
less likely|don't help|fail to help|less help

choice: Which of these is one of the Big Five personality traits?
short: What is the core idea of cognitive behavioural therapy?
Thoughts, feelings and behaviour influence each other, so changing unhelpful thoughts and behaviours changes how you feel.

choice: What is the 'hard problem' of consciousness?
Why physical processes give rise to subjective experience at all
short: After damage to the visual cortex, people respond accurately to things they say they cannot see.

choice: the substance they are made of
short: What is the point of Jackson's Mary's room thought experiment?
Mary knows every physical fact about colour but learns something new when she first sees red, which suggests physicalism leaves something out.

choice: Damage to Broca's area typically causes…
halting speech with relatively good comprehension
short: What does the critical period hypothesis say about language?
Language is acquired most easily in childhood; full native fluency becomes much harder after it.

choice: Searle's Chinese room argument claims that…
running the right program is not enough for understanding
computers can never pass the Turing test
Chinese is harder to process than English
short: What does the Turing test check?
Whether a machine's conversation can be told apart from a human's by an interrogator.

choice: Which empire built the road network and aqueducts across the Mediterranean world?
short: What was Athenian democracy, and who could take part?
Direct rule by the citizens' assembly; only adult male citizens could vote, not women, slaves or foreigners.

choice: What event in 1517 is usually taken as the start of the Reformation?
short: Why did the printing press matter so much?
It made books cheap and fast to copy, spreading ideas, literacy and religious and scientific debate.

choice: Which event is usually seen as the immediate trigger of the First World War?
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
short: A rivalry from 1947 to 1991 between the US and the USSR, fought through arms races, proxy wars and ideology rather than direct war.

choice: In a parliamentary system, the head of government…
depends on the confidence of the legislature
is elected separately from the legislature
cannot be removed before the next election
short: What is the separation of powers?
Splitting government into legislative, executive and judicial branches that check each other.

choice: When a central bank raises interest rates, it usually aims to…
increase unemployment for its own sake
short: The value of the best alternative you give up when you make a choice.

choice: In the Black–Scholes model, which input is not directly observable?
short: What does diversification do to a portfolio?
Combining imperfectly correlated assets lowers risk for the same expected return; only systematic risk remains.

choice: What distinguishes common law from civil law systems?
The weight given to judicial precedent
Whether there are juries in civil cases only
Whether laws are written down at all
short: What does 'innocent until proven guilty' mean in practice?
The prosecution carries the burden of proof, and in criminal cases must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

choice: The smallest sound unit that distinguishes meaning in a language
short: A regular set of consonant shifts from Proto-Indo-European to Proto-Germanic, such as p to f (pater, father).

choice: What did Durkheim's study of suicide argue?
Suicide rates depend on social integration and regulation
Suicide is purely an individual psychological matter
Suicide rates are the same in every society
short: What does 'cultural relativism' mean in anthropology?
Understanding a culture's practices on its own terms rather than judging them by your own culture's standards.

choice: Which is the longest river in South America?
short: Why do cities so often grow up on rivers and coasts?
Water gives drinking water, trade and transport routes, and fertile land.

choice: What does a transistor do in a digital circuit?
Acts as a switch controlled by a small voltage
Stores energy in a magnetic field
short: Why do power grids transmit electricity at high voltage?
For the same power, higher voltage means lower current, so less energy is lost as heat in the lines (losses go as I²R).

choice: What does version control such as Git mainly give you?
A history of changes you can branch, merge and revert
short: A bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of concurrent operations on shared state.

choice: Which technique, developed in Renaissance Florence, made painted space look deep?
Linear perspective with a vanishing point
short: What were the Impressionists trying to capture?
The fleeting effects of light and colour, often painted outdoors with quick, visible brushstrokes.

choice: What structural innovation let Gothic cathedrals have tall walls full of windows?
Flying buttresses carrying the thrust outward
short: A building's or object's shape should come from its purpose rather than from decoration.

choice: Which novel opens with 'Call me Ishmael'?
The Old Man and the Sea
short: A narrator whose account the reader cannot fully trust, through bias, ignorance or deceit.

choice: In equal temperament, how many semitones make up an octave?
short: A contrapuntal piece in which a subject is introduced in one voice and taken up in turn by the others.
What is the 'fourth wall' in theatre?
The imaginary wall between the stage and the audience; breaking it means addressing the audience directly.

choice: What is the Maillard reaction responsible for?
The browning and savoury flavour of seared meat and toast
short: Why do you rest a steak after cooking it?
So the juices redistribute and the temperature evens out, so less liquid runs out when you cut it.

choice: Moving the king two squares towards a rook, which jumps over it
Promoting a pawn on the last rank
short: What is the offside rule in football, roughly?
An attacker is offside if, when the ball is played to them, they are nearer the goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender.

choice: Which band released the album 'Abbey Road'?
short: What is a meme in the original sense, as Dawkins coined it?
A unit of culture, such as an idea or tune, that spreads by imitation, by analogy with a gene.

choice: What does the Ship of Theseus puzzle question?
Whether an object stays the same when all its parts are replaced
short: What is the difference between presentism and eternalism about time?
Presentism says only the present exists; eternalism says past, present and future are all equally real.

choice: The idea that knowledge is justified true belief
The existence of the external world
The possibility of a priori knowledge
short: What is the problem of induction?
We can't justify, without circularity, inferring from past observations to unobserved cases (Hume).

choice: What does a consequentialist judge an action by?
The character of the person acting
short: What is Kant's categorical imperative, in its universal-law form?
Act only on a maxim that you could will to become a universal law.

choice: Behind Rawls's 'veil of ignorance', people choose principles of justice without knowing…
short: The idea that political authority is legitimate because people agree, actually or hypothetically, to give up some freedoms for the protection of a state.

choice: Kant held that a judgement of beauty is…
about the usefulness of the object
short: What counts as art: a mass-produced urinal became art by being chosen and presented as art.

choice: What are the Four Noble Truths a part of?
short: What are the Five Pillars of Islam?
Declaration of faith, prayer, almsgiving, fasting in Ramadan and pilgrimage to Mecca.

choice: Sufism is a mystical tradition within…
short: What is the aim of mindfulness meditation?
Paying attention to present experience, deliberately and without judgement.

choice: In Camus's 'The Myth of Sisyphus', the right response to the absurd is…
revolt: to live fully while knowing life has no inherent meaning
short: What does Sartre mean by 'existence precedes essence'?
There is no given human nature: we exist first and make ourselves through our choices.

choice: Who wrote 'I think, therefore I am'?
short: What is Plato's allegory of the cave about?
Prisoners take shadows for reality; philosophy is the climb out to see the real forms, the truth behind appearances.
